LESSON: ARTICULATION OF LETTER SOUNDS

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: SPEAKING
Topic 2.7: Articulation of Letter Sounds

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Articulation of Letter Sounds. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do different Letter Sounds the learner should be able to: letters of the alphabet on the wall. letters sound?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Demonstrate awareness of letter sounds after the teacher. 3.

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ARTICULATION OF LETTER SOUNDS
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Articulation of Letter Sounds helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: ARTICULATION OF LETTER SOUNDS
Study Articulation of Letter Sounds like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Demonstrate awareness of letter sounds after the teacher. 3.

What this means
In this part you learn to Demonstrate awareness of letter sounds after the teacher. 3.. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Demonstrate awareness of letter sounds after the teacher. 3..
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Articulation of Letter Sounds”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Demonstrate awareness of letter sounds after the teacher. 3.. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Articulation of Letter Sounds is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Articulation of Letter Sounds”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Demonstrate awareness of letter sounds after the teacher. 3.)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Articulation of Letter Sounds to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Demonstrate awareness of letter sounds after the teacher. 3..
3. Make one local Kenya example of Articulation of Letter Sounds from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Articulation of Letter Sounds: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Articulation of Letter Sounds?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do different Letter Sounds the learner should be able to: letters of the alphabet on the wall. letters sound?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Articulation of Letter Sounds means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Demonstrate awareness of letter sounds after the teacher. 3..

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
